summary.title: Arm C Language Extensions
summary.one_liner: The ACLE repository is the source for the Arm C Language Extensions specification, which defines the NEON and SVE intrinsics and how to report defects in them.
keywords: is this compiler behavior a bug
takeaways: The ACLE spec is the reference for what a compiler must accept for NEON and SVE intrinsics, so it is the authority for deciding whether a compiler behavior is a bug.
Arm no longer publishes quarterly releases; the current spec is published after each reviewed change merges into branch main.
Defects and enhancement requests for specs in the repo go to the GitHub issue tracker; documents only on developer.arm.com go to arm.acle@arm.com.
Open-source ACLE documents are licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0 plus a patent grant; legacy closed-source releases use an Arm proprietary license.
The repo also hosts the Morello supplement, Arm MVE intrinsics, Arm Neon intrinsics reference, and the ARMv8-M Security Extensions tools requirements.
summary.summary: This GitHub repository holds the source material from which the Arm C Language Extensions (ACLE) specifications are derived. It explains the versioning model (the current spec is published after each reviewed change merges into main, with legacy quarterly releases through 2026Q1), lists the documents included, and gives the process for reporting defects via GitHub issues. The page is a navigational index rather than a tutorial, and it contains no intrinsic usage details itself.
